title: About
text:
This project combines historical and real-time financial data with AI to produce automated research reports for US growth stock investors. By feeding macroeconomic indicators, equity market data, and commodity prices into an AI model, each report identifies historical patterns, draws parallels to current conditions, and highlights risks and opportunities for growth-oriented portfolios.
All charts and visualizations in the reports are created by the author — the AI generates only the written analysis.

text:
Data Sources
Every report is grounded in real data from:

FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data): Inflation (CPI), GDP growth, unemployment, Fed balance sheet, Treasury yields, household debt, recession indicators, Fed funds rate, and high-yield credit spreads
Yahoo Finance: MSCI World Index, S&P 500, NASDAQ 100, Dow Jones, VIX, gold, and Brent crude oil
Multpl.com: S&P 500 trailing P/E ratios

title: Market Research
text:
Over the past three months leading up to September 11, 2026, global markets have been rattled by a resurgence in inflation risks, driven by a Middle East conflict that pushed Brent crude to $109 a barrel and sent global bond yields spiking toward the 5% mark. Equity leadership has fractured, with the MSCI World Index hovering around 4,937.32 on September 11, 2026, while the Nikkei slumped 2.8%, reflecting a broader risk-off sentiment as investors price in further central bank tightening. Gold has surged past $4,300 an ounce, acting as a hedge against fiscal sustainability concerns and geopolitical instability, echoing the stagflationary anxieties of the late 1970s where commodity shocks repeatedly derailed equity valuations and forced aggressive monetary responses.



MSCI World Equity Index


Domestically, the narrative is equally precarious. The S&P 500 closed at 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq 100 at 29,368.44 on September 11, 2026, masking a deepening divergence under the hood. While headline indices have shown resilience, the macroeconomic tape is flashing warnings that closely mirror the treacherous late-cycle environments of 1978-1979 and 2000.



Performance of Major US Stock Indices


The most immediate threat to long-duration growth assets is the re-emergence of energy-driven inflation. Brent crude reached $104.42 on September 11, 2026, a shock reminiscent of the 1973 and 1979 oil crises. This commodity spike has kept the August 2026 headline CPI anchored at 3.4% YoY, forcing money markets to price in a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike. When the Fed is forced to tighten into an energy shock rather than a booming economy, the discount rate applied to growth stocks rises mechanically. The current S&P 500 P/E ratio of 26.16 on September 11, 2026, leaves little room for error; multiple compression is highly likely if the Fed signals a sustained higher terminal rate, exactly as high-multiple equities suffered in the late 1970s when inflation expectations became unanchored.



Brent Oil Prices


Furthermore, the bond market is signaling that the peak pain may not be in equities, but in the real economy. The 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields settled at 4.41% and 4.82% respectively on September 11, 2026, resulting in a positively sloped yield curve of roughly 41 basis points. Historically, the un-inversion of the yield curve is not a victory lap, but the actual trigger for recessionary damage, much like the curve un-inversions seen in mid-2000 and late-2006. With GDP growth slowing to just 1.5% in Q2 2026 and household debt service payments consuming 11.16% of disposable income in Q1 2026, the consumer is stretched. A cyclical downturn would severely impact the revenue growth trajectories of consumer-discretionary tech and software names that have relied on endless credit expansion.



US 2Y and 10Y Treasury Yields and Spread


Despite these headwinds, the current environment offers distinct opportunities for the disciplined growth investor.

Secular AI Pricing Power: Just as the internet infrastructure boom insulated certain names during the late-1999 macro chop, today’s enterprise AI beneficiaries possess unprecedented pricing power. Companies with entrenched software moats can pass through elevated energy and labor costs without destroying demand. Focusing on free-cash-flow generative tech that is already seeing ROI from AI capex provides a hedge against margin compression.
Strategic Barbell with Hard Assets: With gold trading at $4,390.00 on September 11, 2026, and the Federal Reserve balance sheet still elevated at $6.74 trillion in August 2026, fiscal dominance concerns are validating hard assets. Allocating a portion of the portfolio to gold or short-duration treasuries acts as a volatility dampener. This mirrors the 2000-2002 playbook, where preserving capital in uncorrelated assets allowed investors to aggressively deploy dry powder into growth equities once the inevitable multiple compression finally cleared the froth.




S&P 500 PE Ratio


Given the confluence of an energy-induced inflation shock, a Fed forced back into tightening, and a yield curve that has historically preceded economic contractions, the risk-reward for broad growth equities is currently skewed to the downside. We are likely in the late stages of a cycle where valuations have not yet fully priced in a stagflationary slowdown. Therefore, I suggest maintaining a 25-50% portfolio exposure to U.S. growth stocks. This defensive posture allows us to retain exposure to high-quality, secular AI compounders while hoarding cash and gold to capitalize on the inevitable washout when the macroeconomic reality finally catches up to equity multiples.
